questions.stem: What is Ontology or Knowledge Modelling?
options: The practice of defining a formal, structured representation of knowledge within a domain, including concepts, relationships and rules
The practice of arranging concepts into a simple parent-child hierarchy only
The practice of designing physical storage for documents
The practice of drawing workflow diagrams
The practice of normalising relational tables
questions.explanation: Ontology Modelling defines a formal representation of domain knowledge: important concepts, how they relate and the rules governing those relationships.

questions.stem: What is the main goal of Ontology Modelling?
options: To minimise storage costs
To replace all relational databases
To speed up report rendering
To build a framework supporting semantic clarity, interoperability and reasoning
To classify documents by size
questions.explanation: Ontologies are designed so systems can understand meaning and draw logical conclusions, supporting semantic clarity, interoperability and reasoning.

questions.stem: In the school example, if the ontology states that a Student is a type of Person, what can a system infer about someone who is a Student?
options: That they are also a Teacher
That they attend an Online Course
That they are also a Person
That they teach a Course
Nothing further can be inferred
questions.explanation: Because of the hierarchy, if someone is a Student the system already knows the person is also a Person.

questions.stem: How can an ontology automatically classify a loan as delinquent?
options: By manually tagging each loan
By checking the loan's interest rate
By sorting loans into a taxonomy
By formalising the rule that a Delinquent Loan is a Loan with a missed Repayment, so the system classifies loans when the condition is met
By storing loans in a graph database
questions.explanation: Once the rule Delinquent Loan = Loan with a missed Repayment is formalised, the system can classify loans as delinquent without manual tagging.

questions.stem: What kinds of relationships can elements have in a Data Taxonomy compared with a Data Ontology?
options: Taxonomy elements can have many-to-many relationships; ontology elements only one-to-one
Both allow all relationship types
Neither allows one-to-many relationships
Taxonomy allows one-to-many; ontology allows only one-to-one
Taxonomy elements form only a one-to-one relationship with another element; ontology elements can have one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-one or many-to-many
questions.explanation: In a Data Taxonomy each element forms only a one-to-one relationship with another element, while ontology elements can have all types of relationships.

questions.stem: What are the three key components of an ontology?
options: Tables, Columns and Rows
Nodes, Edges and Weights
Concepts, Relationships and Attributes
Facts, Roles and Sentences
Categories, Tags and Labels
questions.explanation: Ontologies have three key components: Concepts (main kinds of things), Relationships (linking concepts) and Attributes (describing each concept).

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the relationship types listed for ontologies?
options: Hierarchical
Temporal
Causal
Spatial
Alphabetical
questions.explanation: Ontology relationships include Hierarchical, Associative, Dependency, Role-based, Temporal, Causal, Spatial, Equivalence and Disjoint types; alphabetical is not one.

questions.stem: From which Greek roots does the word taxonomy come?
options: taxis meaning order or arrangement, and nomos meaning law or science
techne meaning craft, and logos meaning word
topos meaning place, and nomos meaning name
taxis meaning tax, and onoma meaning name
tele meaning far, and nomos meaning rule
questions.explanation: Taxonomy comes from the Greek taxis, meaning order or arrangement, and nomos, meaning law or science.

questions.stem: Which statement about the relationship between taxonomies and ontologies is correct?
options: Ontologies can be part of taxonomies, but not the other way around
Taxonomies can be part of ontologies, but not the other way around
Taxonomies and ontologies can never be combined
Taxonomies are more advanced than ontologies
Ontologies contain no hierarchies
questions.explanation: Ontology is a more advanced and complex form of taxonomy, so taxonomies can be part of ontologies but not the other way around.

questions.stem: What common mistake is identified regarding structured and unstructured data?
options: Believing unstructured data cannot be analysed
Believing that converting structured data from a table into text format turns it into unstructured data
Believing taxonomies are only for structured data
Believing ontologies replace databases
Believing metadata is optional for unstructured data
questions.explanation: A frequent misconception is that changing a table's format to text makes it unstructured; structured data needs more than a format change to be unstructured.
